Easy Ease is a fine curve. The problem is that it is the same curve every
time, on every property, in every piece, and after a while your work has one
accent.

## What a curve is actually saying

A curve is a claim about weight. A move that starts slowly and arrives quickly
reads as something falling. One that leaves fast and settles slowly reads as
something thrown. Easy Ease sits politely in the middle and says very little.

The fastest way to hear the difference is to keep a move identical and change
only its curve.

:::spec postlab caption="Same distance, same duration. The curve is doing all the talking."

:::

:::more

## Two numbers, and that is most of it

Open the graph editor. You are looking at two handles.

1. **How long the move holds back before it commits.** Drag the first handle
   right and the thing hesitates.
2. **How long it takes to settle at the end.** Drag the second handle left and
   it lands hard, right and it glides in.

Almost everything you like in other people's work is one of those two pushed
further than feels comfortable.

:::note
Overshoot is not a third thing. It is the second handle taken past the value
and allowed to come back. If it feels like a separate trick, you have not
pushed the settle far enough yet.
:::

## The exercise that fixes this fastest

:::do minutes=30
Take one move you already made. Duplicate it three times, side by side. Give
the first a hard landing, the second a long settle, the third a hesitation
before it leaves. Same distance, same duration. Watch all three loop together.
:::

You will pick a favourite within a minute, and it will not be the middle one.

## Where this goes next

Once a single move has a curve you chose, the next question is what happens
when there are five of them, and whether they should share it. That is
spacing, and it is the next piece.
